nodes.name: Trello Board Webhook
nodes.notes: Native Trello webhook on one board. Trello calls this the instant any card/list/checklist action happens — no polling. Watch out: register the webhook against the board ID whose activity you want.

nodes.name: Extract Card & List Fields
nodes.notes: Pulls only the fields worth reporting out of the raw Trello action payload, so downstream nodes never dig into nested webhook JSON.

nodes.name: Keep Creates & Moves
nodes.notes: Drops the noise. Keeps a card creation, or an update that carries a listAfter (i.e. a real move). Renames, comments and due-date edits stop here.

nodes.name: Created or Moved?
nodes.notes: TRUE = a new card (goes to the 'created' wording). FALSE = a move (goes to the 'moved' wording).

nodes.name: Format 'Created' Message
nodes.notes: Builds the Discord text for a newly created card.

nodes.name: Format 'Moved' Message
nodes.notes: Builds the Discord text for a card that changed lists, showing the before → after move.

nodes.name: Post to Discord
nodes.notes: Posts the message to a Discord channel via an incoming webhook — no bot token needed. Retries 3× with backoff; on failure the item exits the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Capture Failure Context
nodes.notes: Error rail: records which card failed to post and why, so nothing is lost when Discord is briefly unavailable.

nodes.name: Alert: Discord Post Failed
nodes.notes: Error rail: posts a fallback notice (ideally to an ops channel) so a swallowed event is visible.

# Post new and moved Trello cards to a Discord channel

**Pattern:** Event → filter → notify · **Level:** Production · **Trigger:** Trello webhook

## What it does
Turns two kinds of Trello board activity — a card being created and a card being moved between lists — into readable Discord messages, and ignores everything else.

## Why it exists
Teams that coordinate in Discord shouldn't have to poll a Trello board to know what changed. This pushes the two events people actually care about into chat, in seconds, with the noise removed.

## Main flow
Trello Board Webhook → Extract Card & List Fields → Keep Creates & Moves → Created or Moved? → Format message → Post to Discord (→ error rail on failure).

## Use it for
- A dev team that watches a sprint board and chats in Discord
- Announcing cards reaching Done without a standup
- Read-only board visibility for stakeholders who don't use Trello

## You get
- Board activity in Discord within seconds
- No noise — only creates and real moves post
- Retried, surfaced failures instead of silent drops

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Trello API; Discord webhook URL.
Colour key: 🟦 entry · 🟫 app I/O · ⬜ logic · 🟩 output · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
This is event-driven: activate it and Trello pushes events to n8n. Sample data is pinned on the trigger, so hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow end to end before attaching a single credential. Right-click → Unpin when you go live.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never bundled in a template. Every node that talks to an external service needs its own connection before the first real run — open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Trello API**
Trello → click your avatar → Power-Ups admin → API key; then authorize a token from the same page. n8n's Trello credential takes the API key + token.
_Gotcha:_ The token must belong to an account that is a member of the board, or every call 401s.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy Webhook URL. Paste it into n8n's Discord Webhook credential.
_Gotcha:_ A webhook URL is bound to one channel. Use a separate webhook/credential per channel you post to.

Set each credential up once; it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Nothing happens when the event should fire**
Cause: The workflow is still a draft, or its trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate it. The manual test URL is different from the production URL.

**A node shows a red triangle right after import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials note).

**Every tiny Trello edit posts to Discord**
Cause: The Filter was widened or removed.
Fix: Keep the Filter: card creates, plus updates that carry a listAfter. That is what makes a move a move.

**Discord posts nothing / returns 400**
Cause: The message content resolved to an empty string, or the webhook URL is wrong.
Fix: Discord rejects empty content. Check the upstream expression produced text, and re-copy the webhook URL.

**The webhook won't register**
Cause: Trello needs a publicly reachable callback URL.
Fix: Activate the workflow so n8n exposes the production URL; Trello rejects localhost callbacks.

Still stuck? The **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there.

## Design decisions

Trello's webhook fires on *every* board action, so filtering is not optional — without the Filter node this would spam the channel on every keystroke. A move is detected by the presence of `listAfter` rather than the action name, because Trello reports a move as a generic `updateCard`. The Discord node runs in webhook mode so no bot has to be invited to the server.

## Practice exercises

Already production-shaped — deepen it:

1. Add a third branch for cards moved *into* a 'Blocked' list and @mention a role.
2. Batch several rapid moves into one digest message using a short Wait + Merge.
3. Post the card's labels and due date by extending the Set node.

## 🛠 Customize me

Watched board is set on **Trello Board Webhook** (`TRELLO_BOARD_ID`). The target channel is whichever webhook URL sits on the Discord credential. Edit the two Set nodes (**Format 'Created'** / **Format 'Moved'**) to change wording or add labels/due dates. To also announce archived cards, add `updateCard` with `closed:true` to **Keep Creates & Moves** and give it its own branch.

## 🔐 Security

The Trello token only needs read access to the one board. The Discord webhook URL is the sole secret on the Discord side — keep it in the credential, never in a node. Card names and member names are posted to Discord, so don't watch a board with confidential card titles unless the channel is private.
